newsitem.title: USA: Jobless claims rise in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Jobless claims rise in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans filing first-time claims for state unemployment benefits rose by 18,000 last week, the Labour Department said Thursday, exceeding economists' expectations.
New filings totalled 340,000 in the week ended Oct. 12, compared with 322,000 in the prior week and above the 331,000 new claims analysts had forecast.
The four-week moving average, a more accurate measurement of employment trends than the more-volatile weekly number, climbed to its highest level since the end of July, moving up 2,750 to 335,750.

The department said 11 states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Oct. 5, the latest period for which the data were available. No states reported decreases in claims in this period.
States reporting the largest increases were California, with 5,361 new claims; Arkansas, with 2,613; Michigan, with 2,546; Florida, with 2,344; New York, with 2,287; and Pennsylvania, with 2,251.

California cited layoffs in the food and service industries and in agriculture. Arkansas had layoffs in the electrical equipment industry, and Florida had layoffs in construction, trade, manufacturing, agriculture and service industries.
Pennsylvania reported layoffs in the service, rubber, and plastics industries. Michigan and New York had no comment.
